question: Kushal and Brijesh together invested ₹37,100 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹12,000, Brijesh's share was ₹5,700. What was the difference between their investments?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Kushal's Profit = Total Profit − Brijesh's Profit = 12000 − 5700 = ₹6,300.

Profit Ratio (Kushal : Brijesh) = 6300 : 5700 = 21 : 19.

Since time is constant, Investment Ratio = Profit Ratio = 21 : 19.

Difference in investment = [(21 − 19) ÷ (21 + 19)] × Total Investment.

Difference = (2 ÷ 40) × 37100 = 3710 ÷ 2 = ₹1,855.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,855.**
